name: ClawEval
intro: Claw-Eval 是面向真实自主 Agent 的可审计端到端评测套件，包含 300 个经人工验证的任务和 2,159 条细粒度 Rubric，通过执行轨迹、服务审计日志和环境快照评估完成度、安全性、鲁棒性与多次运行可靠性。
org: Peking University, The University of Hong Kong
build_method: 250个原创任务+50个兼容任务, 运行环境与Rubric实现, 独立复核, 前沿模型试跑
metric: Average Score, Pass@3, Pass^3, Completion, Safety, Robustness
modality: 文本, 图像, 视频, 代码
task_type: 工作流Agent任务, 多模态任务, 多轮专业对话
eval_feature: 全轨迹审计, 三证据通道, 时间防火墙, 受控错误注入, 三次独立运行
task_type_en: Workflow agent tasks, multimodal tasks, multi-turn professional dialogue
build_method_en: 250 original plus 50 compatibility tasks, runtime and rubric implementation, independent review, and frontier-model pilot validation
eval_feature_en: Full-trajectory auditing, three evidence channels, temporal firewall, controlled error injection, three independent trials
intro_en: Claw-Eval is an auditable end-to-end suite for real-world autonomous agents. Its 300 human-verified tasks and 2,159 fine-grained rubrics use execution traces, service audit logs, and environment snapshots to evaluate completion, safety, robustness, and multi-run reliability.
metric_en: Average Score, Pass@3, Pass^3, Completion, Safety, Robustness
drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2604.06132, especially Sections 3.1-3.3 and Appendices B-D. The released suite has 300 human-verified tasks: 161 General, 101 Multimodal, and 38 Multi-turn tasks across nine categories. Authors create 250 original tasks and adapt 50 compatibility tasks while preserving source prompts and scoring semantics; they implement sandbox assets, mock services or simulated users and 2,159 deterministic or judgment-based rubric items. A second author reviews correctness, completeness and leakage, and multiple frontier models pilot-test difficulty and rubric discrimination before release. Each evaluation uses a fresh Docker sandbox and a temporal firewall separating Setup, Execution and Judge phases. Grading is grounded in execution traces, service-side audit logs and post-execution environment snapshots. Completion and robustness are combined under a multiplicative safety gate, with controlled error injection and three trials supporting Average Score, Pass@3 and Pass^3.
